name: SGLang hardware-dependent kernel selection logic for FP4/FP8 GEMM
bits: varies by backend - W4A16 (Marlin), W4A4 (NVFP4), W8A8 (FP8)
activation_scheme: Depends on the selected backend. The kernel selection is based on hardware compute capability and the quantization format of the checkpoint.
kernels: Marlin (W4A16 fallback for NVFP4 on SM80-SM90)
FlashInfer cuDNN (NVFP4 on SM100/SM120, CUDA 13+, cuDNN 9.15+)
notes: CRITICAL KERNEL SELECTION LOGIC: SGLang's --fp4-gemm-backend auto-selection order is: 1) flashinfer_cutedsl on SM100, 2) marlin on SM80-SM90, 3) flashinfer_cutlass otherwise (including SM120). This means that on SM80-SM90 (Ampere/Hopper), an NVFP4 checkpoint will be served with Marlin, which is a W4A16 kernel - the FP4 weights are dequantized to FP16 and the FP4 activations are upcast to FP16. The NVFP4 format is effectively treated as W4A16 on pre-Blackwell hardware. This is a SILENT PRECISION DEGRADATION: the user loads an NVFP4 model expecting 4-bit x 4-bit compute, but gets 4-bit weight storage with FP16 compute. The memory saving materializes but the compute speedup does not. On SM100 (Blackwell), the native NVFP4 path is used. For FP8: auto-selection is 1) DeepGEMM (SM90/SM100, if installed), 2) FlashInfer TRTLLM (SM100), 3) CUTLASS (SM120), 4) AITER (AMD), 5) Triton (fallback). MXFP8 dense linear uses flashinfer_cutlass on SM100, else triton. The platform compatibility table shows that modelopt_fp4 uses 'Marlin W4A16 fallback on Ampere/Hopper and native FP4 backends on Blackwell'. This is the documented case where the WRONG kernel gets picked because a format (NVFP4) is classified as weight-only when it is actually weight-and-activation - on pre-Blackwell hardware, the activation quantization is silently dropped.
